Can AI help power a Just Energy Future?

Today, we stand at a crossroads. ChatGPT now reaches over 400 million weekly users, yet 1.18 billion people still live without reliable energy access. This paradox highlights both the promise and the peril of AI: it can deepen divides, or it can help us build more efficient, resilient and equitable energy systems.

In this piece, co-written with my colleague Stefano Pistolese , we argue that a new paradigm, “planetary intelligence” is emerging. By learning from nature and managing systems holistically, AI has the potential to transform not just energy, but the interconnected challenges of water, land, biodiversity and culture. To seize this opportunity, we must act on three fronts:

1️⃣ Move from biomimicry to “machine ecology”: AI can shift from copying nature’s designs to managing energy like an ecosystem. Smart grids already cut losses by 20%, and predictive tools balance renewables in real time. At scale, this could cut emissions 10% by 2030 and expand access.

2️⃣ Scale ecosystem-level solutions: AI modeled on natural systems can manage trade-offs across water, land, and biodiversity, creating up to $1.3 trillion in value by 2030 while safeguarding planetary health.

3️⃣ Ground innovation in equity: Efforts like Masakhane’s 40 African language models show how planetary intelligence can reflect diverse cultures, widening who benefits from AI and ensuring inclusion in the energy transition.

The question is not if AI will reshape our energy future, but how - and whether it will do so in a way that serves all people, not just a few. With the right governance, AI can become a catalyst for just and sustainable development.
